matched_126.excluded_reason: OpenSLT could not produce a prediction for these 2 clips; excluded from this scope so the comparison against OpenSLT/Uni-Sign below is apples-to-apples on the identical clip set.

apples_to_apples_comparison_matched_126.interpretation_caveat: Curify's WER (0.9761) is numerically between OpenSLT's (1.0246) and Uni-Sign's (0.9801) but this must NOT be read as 'Curify outperforms Uni-Sign.' Uni-Sign's BLEU (5.40) is ~40x Curify's (0.1346) and its chrF (22.83) is roughly double Curify's (11.30) -- both far more sensitive than WER to whether the *content* of the output is actually correct. WER alone is a weak signal here because Curify's error profile is deletion-dominated (see deletion_dominance below): a system that outputs very few words can post a deceptively competitive WER purely by avoiding substitution opportunities, without saying anything correct.

deletion_dominance_evidence.interpretation: Curify predictions average 41% of the reference length. Deletions account for 61% of all edit operations vs. 38% substitutions and 1% insertions -- the model is systematically truncating/omitting content rather than mis-describing it, consistent with the qualitative pattern of short, thin outputs.

temporal_recall_vs_precision.interpretation: Very high precision (0.99) with much lower recall (0.58) means that when Curify does emit a segment, it is almost always aligned to genuine reference signing time (few false-positive time spans), but it only covers ~58% of the total reference signing duration -- consistent with the deletion-dominant text pattern: the model is silent/skipping across a large fraction of the video rather than misplacing its guesses in time.

flagged_clip_frozen_prediction.note: This is the only value to use. An earlier ad-hoc 'Tuberculosis / Drive / Nice' output for this clip is NOT from the frozen saved baseline and must not be cited.
